# Script introduction

This is the last of six R Markdown notebooks. It turns the fitted models and checks into the summaries and figures of the report: the robustness table, residual autocorrelation, the counts quoted in the text, the Supporting Information tables, Figures 1-4 and Figures S1, S2 and S4-S8 (Figure S3 is drawn in `s05_check_robustness`).

The inputs are the trait table and evidence ledger of `s01_prepare_traits`, the occurrence records, range metrics and validation tables of `s02_prepare_ranges`, the species tables and Daru range cells of `s03_build_species_tables`, the model tables of `s04_fit_models`, the rarefied-range models of `s05_check_robustness` and the Yumnam & Kodandaramaiah (2025) tree. All outputs are read by the report, which includes the figures from `results/s06_summarise_results/`. A full run takes about 10 min.

# Setup

## Packages

`ggplot2` and `patchwork` draw the figures and `sf` the maps; `ape`, `lme4`, `ragg`, `reformulas`, `rnaturalearth` and `scales` are called with `::`.

```{r load_packages, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(resrepo)
library(data.table)
library(lmerTest)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(sf)
```

## Variables

The three range measures, the labels of the two species tables in the model tables, and the colours shared by the figures are fixed here.

```{r setup_variables}
# Range measures: short name -> column of the species table
measures <- c(area = "range_area", lat = "latitudinal_extent", lon = "longitudinal_extent")

# Labels of the two species tables in the `table` column of the s04 model tables
main_table <- "MAIN_subtype"
daru_table <- "MAIN_daru_subtype"

# Colours of the interaction types
type_colours <- c(n = "#4D4D4D", f = "#0072B2", m = "#E69F00", p = "#CC79A7")

# Sequential palette of the maps (light = low, dark = high)
magma_colours <- c("#FCFDBF", "#FC8961", "#B73779", "#51127C", "#000004")
```

The species tables are read in several sections, and every figure is saved in the same way.

```{r define_helpers}
# Read a species table of s03 as a data frame, with the given key columns read as text and the
# interaction types as a factor
read_species_table <- function(file = "species_table.csv", key_columns = "pool_key") {
  d <- read.csv(file.path(dir_s03, file),
                na.strings = c("", "NA"),
                colClasses = setNames(rep("character", length(key_columns)), key_columns))
  d$interaction_type <- factor(d$interaction_type, levels = c("n", "f", "m", "p"))
  d
}

# Save a report figure as a PNG in this notebook's folder; ragg (AGG) renders text identically on
# every machine, which the base png() device does not. `name` is the file name without the
# extension; width and height are in inches.
save_report_figure <- function(plot, name, width, height, dpi = 300) {
  ggsave(file.path(dir_data_intermediate, paste0(name, ".png")), plot,
         width = width, height = height, dpi = dpi, bg = "white", device = ragg::agg_png)
}
```

The maps of Figures 1, S4, S5 and S6 share three functions: Equal Earth cells become polygons (Figure S6 builds its cells from their ids), the polygons are clipped to land, and each panel is drawn in the same style.

```{r define_map_functions}
#' Convert equal-area Equal Earth cells to map polygons
#'
#' Cells of `cell_km` x `cell_km` in the Equal Earth projection all have the same area on
#' the ground (unlike longitude-latitude cells, which shrink towards the poles). Cell indices
#' are those of `equal_area_species_cells()`: the lower-left corner is `cell_x * cell_km` km
#' east and `cell_y * cell_km` km north in the projection.
#' @param cells Data frame with integer columns `cell_x` and `cell_y`; other columns are kept.
#' @param cell_km Cell side in km (the value used to create the indices).
#' @return sf polygons in the Equal Earth CRS of `global_equal_area_crs()`.
equal_area_cell_polygons <- function(cells, cell_km = 250) {
  stopifnot(all(c("cell_x", "cell_y") %in% names(cells)), is.finite(cell_km), cell_km > 0)
  s <- cell_km * 1000

  # One closed square (five corners, starting at the lower-left one) per cell
  geometries <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(cells)), function(i) {
    x0 <- cells$cell_x[i] * s
    y0 <- cells$cell_y[i] * s
    sf::st_polygon(list(rbind(c(x0, y0), c(x0 + s, y0), c(x0 + s, y0 + s),
                              c(x0, y0 + s), c(x0, y0))))
  })
  sf::st_sf(cells, geometry = sf::st_sfc(geometries, crs = global_equal_area_crs()))
}

#' Prepare land and gridded data for publication maps
#'
#' The cells are transformed to Equal Earth and clipped to land, so that coastal
#' cells do not colour the sea. Unoccupied land remains grey and the panel
#' background supplies the light-blue ocean.
#' @param cells sf polygons of the 500-km Equal Earth cells (e.g. from
#'   `equal_area_cell_polygons()`).
#' @return A list with projected `cells` and `land` layers.
map_layers <- function(cells) {
  # Land and cells in the Equal Earth projection
  target <- global_equal_area_crs()
  land <- rnaturalearth::ne_countries(scale = "small", returnclass = "sf")
  land <- sf::st_make_valid(sf::st_transform(land[, "geometry"], target))
  cells <- sf::st_make_valid(sf::st_transform(cells, target))

  # Unioning first avoids duplicating coastal grid fragments at country borders.
  clipped <- suppressWarnings(sf::st_intersection(cells, sf::st_union(land)))
  list(cells = clipped, land = land)
}

#' Draw one publication map in Equal Earth
#'
#' @param layers Output from `map_layers()`.
#' @param variable Column in `layers$cells` to map.
#' @param title Legend title.
#' @param palette Colours of the sequential scale, or low, mid and high colours of a
#'   diverging scale.
#' @param trans Scale transformation, usually `identity` or `log10`.
#' @param midpoint Optional midpoint for a diverging scale.
#' @param limits Optional limits of the colour scale; values outside them take the end colour.
#' @param breaks Optional scale breaks; defaults to ggplot2's automatic choice.
#' @param labels Optional labels for `breaks` (sequential scale only), e.g. to mark a truncated
#'   end ("≤ 0.5") when values outside `limits` are squished onto it.
#' @return A ggplot object.
plot_grid_map <- function(layers, variable, title, palette,
                          trans = "identity", midpoint = NULL, limits = NULL,
                          breaks = ggplot2::waiver(), labels = ggplot2::waiver()) {
  # Cells with a finite value (and a positive one on a log scale)
  values <- layers$cells[[variable]]
  keep <- is.finite(values) & (trans != "log10" | values > 0)
  cells <- layers$cells[keep, , drop = FALSE]
  cells$value <- cells[[variable]]

  # Colour scale: sequential, or diverging when a midpoint is given
  scale <- if (is.null(midpoint)) {
    ggplot2::scale_fill_gradientn(
      colours = palette,
      trans = trans, limits = limits, breaks = breaks, labels = labels,
      oob = scales::squish, name = title,
      na.value = NA,
      guide = ggplot2::guide_colourbar(title.position = "top", title.hjust = 0.5,
                                       barwidth = grid::unit(35, "mm"),
                                       barheight = grid::unit(3, "mm")))
  } else {
    ggplot2::scale_fill_gradient2(
      low = palette[1], mid = palette[2], high = palette[3],
      midpoint = midpoint, limits = limits, oob = scales::squish,
      breaks = breaks, name = title, na.value = NA,
      guide = ggplot2::guide_colourbar(title.position = "top", title.hjust = 0.5,
                                       barwidth = grid::unit(35, "mm"),
                                       barheight = grid::unit(3, "mm")))
  }

  # Grey land, the cells on top of it, then the country outlines
  ggplot2::ggplot() +
    ggplot2::geom_sf(data = layers$land, fill = "grey55", colour = "grey35",
                     linewidth = 0.08) +
    ggplot2::geom_sf(data = cells, ggplot2::aes(fill = value), colour = NA) +
    ggplot2::geom_sf(data = layers$land, fill = NA, colour = "grey25", linewidth = 0.08) +

    # Colour scale, projection and axis labels
    scale +
    ggplot2::coord_sf(crs = global_equal_area_crs(), expand = FALSE,
                      label_axes = list(bottom = "E", left = "N")) +
    ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +

    # Minimal theme with a light-blue ocean and a colour bar above the map
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
    ggplot2::theme(
      panel.background = ggplot2::element_rect(fill = "#ADD8E6", colour = NA),
      panel.grid.major = ggplot2::element_line(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2),
      panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(),

      legend.position = "top",
      legend.title = ggplot2::element_text(size = 8),
      legend.text = ggplot2::element_text(size = 7),

      axis.title = ggplot2::element_text(size = 8),
      axis.text = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      axis.ticks = ggplot2::element_blank(),

      plot.margin = ggplot2::margin(2, 3, 2, 3)
    )
}
```

# Main-model summaries and Figure 2

The main models are refitted (they must equal the saved fits) to build the robustness table: the main mixed model beside the spherical GAM, the all-butterfly background, the 80-95 % range-stability subsets, Daru modelled ranges, matched-tip, genus-grafted and genus-level PGLS, the joint phylogenetic spatial model and a wingspan covariate. The section also writes Moran's I of the range-area residuals between species centres within 500 and 1,000 km, the counts quoted in the text, and Figure 2 (species' ranges by interaction type with the model estimates).

*Inputs:* s03/ species_table.csv, species_table_daru.csv, analysis_units.csv, daru_all_species.csv, daru_cells_500km.csv; s04/ main_models.rds, main_contrasts.csv, main_estimated_means.csv, main_metadata.csv, lmm_\*, gam_\*, background_\*, pgls_matched_\*, pgls_grafted_\*, genus_level_pgls.csv, phylo_geography_contrasts.csv, species_centres.csv, presence_500km.csv; s02/ range_metrics.csv, dataset_counts.csv, expert_validation_summary.csv; s01/species_traits.csv  
*Outputs:* robustness.csv, pgls_metadata.csv, wingspan_coefficients.csv, residual_moran.csv, counts.csv, plot_range_by_interaction_type.png (Figure 2)

```{r read_main_table}
# Main species table of s03
d <- read_species_table()
```

## Main models

The main models are refitted because the robustness rows and residual checks need the fitted objects and their samples; they must equal the saved main models.

```{r refit_main_models}
# Refit the main models and compare their type contrasts with the saved ones of s04
fit <- fit_log_range_models(d, measures = measures, breadth_scale = "raw")
ref <- fread(file.path(dir_s04, "main_contrasts.csv"))
chk <- merge(as.data.table(fit$contrasts)[, .(measure, predictors, contrast,
                                              r1 = range_ratio)],
             ref[, .(measure, predictors, contrast, r2 = range_ratio)],
             by = c("measure", "predictors", "contrast"))
stopifnot(nrow(chk) == nrow(ref), max(abs(chk$r1 / chk$r2 - 1)) < 1e-8)
```

## Robustness table

```{r robustness_table}
# --- Helpers that put a model table in the robustness-table layout ---
# Type contrasts of a model table, as "a-b"; n-f is shown as f-n (its ratio and interval
# inverted). Returns measure, contrast, ratio, lower, upper and p.
flip <- function(x) {
  x <- as.data.table(x)[, contrast := gsub(" ", "", contrast)]
  i <- x$contrast == "n-f"
  x[i, `:=`(contrast = "f-n",
            range_ratio = 1 / range_ratio,
            lo = 1 / ratio_upper,
            hi = 1 / ratio_lower)]
  x[!i, `:=`(lo = ratio_lower, hi = ratio_upper)]
  x[, .(measure, contrast, ratio = range_ratio, lower = lo, upper = hi, p = p.value)]
}

# Partner-breadth slope of a coefficient table, in the same layout
slope <- function(x)
  as.data.table(x)[predictors == "breadth" & term == "partner_breadth_centered",
                   .(measure, contrast = "breadth", ratio = range_ratio,
                     lower = ratio_lower, upper = ratio_upper, p = p_value)]

# Read a model table of s04
read_s04 <- function(file) fread(file.path(dir_s04, file))

# --- Model tables of s04 (c: contrasts, k: coefficients, m: metadata) ---
# Taxonomic mixed models (the main model, its range-stability subsets and the Daru table)
lmm_c <- read_s04("lmm_contrasts.csv")
lmm_k <- read_s04("lmm_coefficients.csv")
lmm_m <- read_s04("lmm_metadata.csv")

# Spherical GAMs
gam_c <- read_s04("gam_contrasts.csv")
gam_k <- read_s04("gam_coefficients.csv")
gam_m <- read_s04("gam_metadata.csv")

# All-butterfly regional background models
reg_c <- read_s04("background_contrasts.csv")
reg_k <- read_s04("background_coefficients.csv")
reg_m <- read_s04("background_metadata.csv")

# Phylogenetic models: the two trees shown in the report, on matched tips (pg) and on
# genus-grafted trees (gr)
report_trees <- c("yumnam_2025", "schar_2018")
pg_c <- read_s04("pgls_matched_contrasts.csv")
pg_k <- read_s04("pgls_matched_coefficients.csv")
pg_m <- read_s04("pgls_matched_metadata.csv")
gr_c <- read_s04("pgls_grafted_contrasts.csv")
gr_k <- read_s04("pgls_grafted_coefficients.csv")
gr_m <- read_s04("pgls_grafted_metadata.csv")

# --- Helpers that assemble the rows of one analysis ---
# One analysis in the robustness-table layout: its type contrasts and breadth slope, with the
# sample size and number of parasites. `ct`, `co` and `md` are the contrast, coefficient and
# metadata tables of the analysis; `n_par` supplies the parasite numbers when the metadata do
# not record them (a number, or a list with the entries `type` and `breadth`).
one <- function(label, ct, co, md, n_par = NA_integer_) {
  # Contrasts and breadth slope
  r <- rbind(flip(ct[predictors == "type"]), slope(co))

  # Sample size (and parasite number, where recorded) of each model
  nn <- md[, .(n = n[1],
               n_parasite_model = if ("n_parasite" %in% names(md)) n_parasite[1]
                                  else NA_integer_),
           by = .(measure, predictors)]
  r[, n := ifelse(contrast == "breadth",
                  nn$n[match(paste(measure, "breadth"), paste(nn$measure, nn$predictors))],
                  nn$n[match(paste(measure, "type"), paste(nn$measure, nn$predictors))])]

  # Parasite numbers differ between type and breadth samples; phylogenetic
  # metadata already records both, while full LMM fits supply them explicitly.
  pred_key <- ifelse(r$contrast == "breadth", "breadth", "type")
  np <- nn$n_parasite_model[match(paste(r$measure, pred_key),
                                  paste(nn$measure, nn$predictors))]
  fallback <- if (is.list(n_par)) vapply(pred_key, function(k) n_par[[k]], 1L) else
    rep(n_par, nrow(r))
  np[is.na(np)] <- fallback[is.na(np)]
  r[, `:=`(analysis = label, n_parasite = np)]
  r
}

# Number of parasites in the range-area type and breadth samples of a fit_log_range_models() fit
npar <- function(fitobj)
  list(type = sum(fitobj$model_data$area_type$interaction_type == "p"),
       breadth = sum(fitobj$model_data$area_breadth$interaction_type == "p"))

# --- Robustness table ---
# One block of rows per analysis
robust <- rbind(
  # Main taxonomic mixed model
  one("lmm",
      lmm_c[table == main_table & analysis == "main"],
      lmm_k[table == main_table & analysis == "main"],
      lmm_m[table == main_table & analysis == "main"],
      npar(fit)),

  # Spherical GAM
  one("spherical_gam",
      gam_c[table == main_table],
      gam_k[table == main_table],
      gam_m[table == main_table]),

  # All-butterfly regional background
  one("background_500km_butterflies",
      reg_c[table == main_table & analysis == "regional_background_500_bfly"],
      reg_k[table == main_table & analysis == "regional_background_500_bfly"],
      reg_m[table == main_table & analysis == "regional_background_500_bfly"]),

  # Range-stability subsets (80, 90 and 95 %)
  one("stability_80",
      lmm_c[table == main_table & analysis == "stability_80"],
      lmm_k[table == main_table & analysis == "stability_80"],
      lmm_m[table == main_table & analysis == "stability_80"]),
  one("stability_90",
      lmm_c[table == main_table & analysis == "stability_90"],
      lmm_k[table == main_table & analysis == "stability_90"],
      lmm_m[table == main_table & analysis == "stability_90"]),
  one("stability_95",
      lmm_c[table == main_table & analysis == "stability_95"],
      lmm_k[table == main_table & analysis == "stability_95"],
      lmm_m[table == main_table & analysis == "stability_95"]),

  # Daru modelled ranges
  one("modelled_ranges_daru",
      lmm_c[table == daru_table & analysis == "main"],
      lmm_k[table == daru_table & analysis == "main"],
      lmm_m[table == daru_table & analysis == "main"]),

  # Matched-tip PGLS, one block per tree
  rbindlist(lapply(report_trees, function(s) {
    m <- pg_m[table == main_table & study == s]
    one(paste0("pgls_", s),
        pg_c[table == main_table & study == s],
        pg_k[table == main_table & study == s],
        m,
        m[measure == "area" & predictors == "type", n_parasite])
  })),

  # Genus-grafted trees: the main phylogenetic analysis
  rbindlist(lapply(report_trees, function(s) {
    m <- gr_m[study == s]
    one(paste0("pgls_grafted_", s),
        gr_c[study == s],
        gr_k[study == s],
        m,
        m[measure == "area" & predictors == "type", n_parasite])
  })),
  fill = TRUE)

# --- Wingspan covariate ---
# Wingspan sensitivity: the main models plus log10 wingspan (measured values only; genus-median
# imputations excluded) as a centred covariate. fit_log_range_models() takes one centred species
# covariate through its regional-background argument, so log10 wingspan is passed in those
# columns (same centring, estimated means at the mean, Tukey contrasts as every other row).
wing_ok <- is.finite(d$wingspan_mm) & d$wingspan_mm > 0 &
  !d$wingspan_basis %in% "imputed_genus_median"
dw <- d[wing_ok, ]
for (m in names(measures)) dw[[paste0("regional_background_", m)]] <- log10(dw$wingspan_mm)
fit_w <- fit_log_range_models(dw, measures = measures, regional_background = TRUE,
                              breadth_scale = "raw")

# Coefficient of the covariate, written to its own table
wing_coef <- as.data.table(fit_w$coefficients)[term == "regional_background_centered"]
wing_coef[, term := "log10_wingspan_centered"]
write_table(wing_coef, file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "wingspan_coefficients.csv"))

# Rows of the model with the covariate
robust <- rbind(robust,
                one("wingspan_covariate",
                    as.data.table(fit_w$contrasts),
                    as.data.table(fit_w$coefficients),
                    as.data.table(fit_w$metadata),
                    npar(fit_w)),
                fill = TRUE)

# --- Genus-level PGLS ---
# All genera: one unit per genus x interaction type, so n = genus units and n_parasite =
# parasitic genus units; type contrasts only.
glv <- read_s04("genus_level_pgls.csv")[dropped == "none" & tree %in% report_trees]
robust <- rbind(robust,
                glv[, .(analysis = paste0("pgls_genus_", tree), measure, contrast,
                        n = n_units, n_parasite = n_p_units, ratio, lower, upper, p)],
                fill = TRUE)

# --- Joint phylogenetic spatial model ---
# With all its contrasts
joint <- read_s04("phylo_geography_contrasts.csv")[model == "phylo_spatial_gam"]
joint[, contrast := gsub(" ", "", contrast)]
joint[contrast == "n-f",
      `:=`(contrast = "f-n", ratio = 1 / ratio, lower = 1 / upper, upper = 1 / lower)]
robust <- rbind(robust,
                joint[, .(analysis = paste0("phylo_spatial_", study), measure, contrast,
                          n, n_parasite, ratio, lower, upper, p)],
                fill = TRUE)

# --- Parasites of the remaining analyses ---
# Parasites in the type-model samples whose metadata do not record them: the same sample filter
# as fit_log_range_models(), checked against the stored sample size. Returns the sample size
# and the number of parasites of the species table `dd`; `threshold` keeps only species whose
# range stability for the measure `label` exceeds it.
sample_parasites <- function(dd, label, threshold = NULL) {
  if (!is.null(threshold)) {
    st <- dd[[paste0("asympt_prop_", label)]]
    dd <- dd[is.finite(st) & st > threshold, , drop = FALSE]
  }

  # Species with a positive range, a type, a genus and a subfamily
  r <- dd[[measures[[label]]]]
  dd <- dd[is.finite(r) & r > 0 & !is.na(dd$interaction_type) & !is.na(dd$genus) &
             !is.na(dd$subfamily), , drop = FALSE]
  c(n = nrow(dd), p = sum(dd$interaction_type == "p"))
}

# Fill the missing parasite numbers of the type contrasts of one analysis in `robust` (by
# reference), using the species table `dd` behind that analysis
fill_parasites <- function(label, dd, threshold = NULL) {
  for (m in names(measures)) {
    i <- which(robust$analysis == label & robust$measure == m &
                 robust$contrast != "breadth" & is.na(robust$n_parasite))
    if (!length(i)) next
    s <- sample_parasites(dd, m, threshold)
    stopifnot(all(robust$n[i] == s[["n"]]))
    set(robust, i, "n_parasite", as.integer(s[["p"]]))
  }
}

# Spherical GAM, all-butterfly background, Daru ranges and the stability subsets
fill_parasites("spherical_gam", d)
fill_parasites("background_500km_butterflies", d)
fill_parasites("modelled_ranges_daru", read_species_table("species_table_daru.csv"))
for (s in c(80, 90, 95)) fill_parasites(paste0("stability_", s), d, s / 100)

# --- Write the tables ---
setcolorder(robust, c("analysis", "measure", "contrast", "n", "n_parasite"))
write_table(robust, file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "robustness.csv"))

# Metadata of the phylogenetic models (matched and genus-grafted trees)
write_table(rbind(cbind(pg_m[table == main_table & study %in% report_trees],
                        tree_set = "matched"),
                  gr_m[study %in% report_trees],
                  fill = TRUE),
            file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "pgls_metadata.csv"))
```

## Residual spatial autocorrelation

Moran's I of the range-area type-model residuals between species centres within 500 and 1,000 km is computed for the main model, the model with the all-butterfly background (rebuilt here for its residuals) and the spherical GAM.

```{r residual_moran}
# --- Species centres and 500-km presence cells ---
ce <- fread(file.path(dir_s04, "species_centres.csv"),
            colClasses = c(species = "character"))
r26 <- read.csv(file.path(dir_s02, "range_metrics.csv"),
                colClasses = c(pool_key = "character"))
r26 <- r26[!duplicated(r26$pool_key) & is.finite(r26$range_area), ]
p5 <- read.csv(file.path(dir_s04, "presence_500km.csv"),
               colClasses = c(species = "character"))
p5 <- p5[p5$species %in% r26$pool_key, ]

# --- All-butterfly background, rebuilt for its residuals ---
# The genus left out of a unit's background is its revised genus as an analysis unit, else its
# GBIF genus.
units <- read.csv(file.path(dir_s03, "analysis_units.csv"),
                  colClasses = c(pool_key = "character"))
unit_genus <- units$genus[match(r26$pool_key, units$pool_key)]
bg5 <- butterfly_range_background(
  p5,
  setNames(ifelse(is.na(unit_genus), r26$genus, unit_genus), r26$pool_key),
  fread(file.path(dir_s03, "daru_all_species.csv")),
  fread(file.path(dir_s03, "daru_cells_500km.csv")),
  measures = measures)

# Range-area model with the background as a covariate
db <- d
for (cc in grep("^regional_background_", names(bg5), value = TRUE))
  db[[cc]] <- ifelse(is.finite(db$range_area),
                     bg5[[cc]][match(db$pool_key, bg5$species)],
                     NA)
fit_bg <- fit_log_range_models(db, measures = c(area = "range_area"),
                               regional_background = TRUE, breadth_scale = "raw")

# The f - p range-area ratio must equal that of the saved background model
r_bg <- as.data.table(fit_bg$contrasts)[predictors == "type" & contrast == "f - p",
                                        range_ratio]
r_bg0 <- reg_c[table == main_table & analysis == "regional_background_500_bfly" &
                 measure == "area" & predictors == "type" & contrast == "f - p",
               range_ratio]
stopifnot(abs(r_bg / r_bg0 - 1) < 1e-8)   # same background model as in s04_fit_models

# --- Spherical GAM of range area ---
dg <- merge(as.data.frame(d), ce, by.x = "pool_key", by.y = "species")
gam <- fit_species_spatial_gam(dg, "range_area")

# --- Moran's I of the residuals ---
# Moran's I of the residuals `res` of a model fitted to the units `keys`, between species centres
# within 500 and 1,000 km. The weights are 1 for pairs of centres at a distance above 0 and up to
# the cut-off. Returns one row per cut-off.
moran <- function(label, keys, res) {
  k <- match(keys, ce$species)
  ok <- !is.na(k)
  D <- gc_km(ce$geo_latitude[k[ok]], ce$geo_longitude[k[ok]])
  rbindlist(lapply(c(500, 1000), function(cut) {
    m <- ape::Moran.I(res[ok], (D > 0 & D <= cut) * 1)
    data.table(model = label, distance_km = cut, n = sum(ok), moran_i = m$observed,
               expected = m$expected, p = m$p.value)
  }))
}

# Main model, model with the all-butterfly background, and spherical GAM
mor <- rbind(
  moran("lmm", fit$model_data$area_type$pool_key, residuals(fit$models$area_type)),
  moran("background_500km_butterflies", fit_bg$model_data$area_type$pool_key,
        residuals(fit_bg$models$area_type)),
  moran("spherical_gam", gam$data$pool_key, residuals(gam$model)))
write_table(mor, file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "residual_moran.csv"))
print(mor)
```

## Figure 2

```{r plot_figure_2}
# Species' observed ranges by interaction type (violins and boxes of the type-model samples) with
# the model-estimated means and intervals offset beside them. Drawn from the saved main models
# and their tables, as read by the report (the compact letters depend on the tables' row order
# and formats).

# --- Saved main models and tables ---
main_models <- readRDS(file.path(dir_s04, "main_models.rds"))
estimated_means <- read.csv(file.path(dir_s04, "main_estimated_means.csv"))
main_contrasts <- read.csv(file.path(dir_s04, "main_contrasts.csv"))
main_metadata <- read.csv(file.path(dir_s04, "main_metadata.csv"))

# --- Compact letters ---
# Compact letters of the Tukey-adjusted contrasts: types that share a letter do not differ at
# p < 0.05, which does not establish that they are equivalent. Returns the letters of each type
# as a named character vector; `contrasts` and `means` are the contrast and estimated-mean
# tables of one measure.
compact_letters <- function(contrasts, means) {
  # Types from the largest to the smallest estimated mean
  groups <- as.character(means$interaction_type[order(-means$emmean)])

  # TRUE when the contrast between types a and b is not significant
  non_significant <- function(a, b) {
    p <- contrasts$p.value[
      contrasts$contrast %in% c(paste(a, "-", b), paste(b, "-", a))
    ]
    stopifnot(length(p) == 1L, is.finite(p))
    p >= 0.05
  }

  # Sets of types in which no pair differs, then the maximal ones, ordered by the rank of
  # their first type
  combinations <- unlist(lapply(seq_along(groups), function(k)
    combn(groups, k, simplify = FALSE)), recursive = FALSE)
  cliques <- Filter(function(s) length(s) == 1L ||
    all(combn(s, 2L, function(pair) non_significant(pair[1], pair[2]))),
    combinations)
  maximal <- Filter(function(s) !any(vapply(cliques, function(t)
    length(t) > length(s) && all(s %in% t), logical(1))), cliques)
  maximal <- maximal[order(vapply(maximal, function(s)
    min(match(s, groups)), numeric(1)))]

  # One letter per maximal set, added to every type in the set
  labels <- setNames(rep("", length(groups)), groups)
  for (i in seq_along(maximal)) labels[maximal[[i]]] <-
    paste0(labels[maximal[[i]]], letters[i])
  labels
}

# --- Panels, one per range measure ---
titles <- c(area = "Range area (km²)", lat = "Latitudinal extent (km)",
            lon = "Longitudinal extent (km)")
type_labels <- c(n = "Non-ant-associated", f = "Facultative", m = "Obligate mutualist",
                 p = "Obligate parasite")
panels <- lapply(names(titles), function(measure) {
  # Observations of the type model, checked against the stored sample size
  frame <- stats::model.frame(main_models[[paste0(measure, "_type")]])
  expected_n <- main_metadata$n[main_metadata$measure == measure &
                                  main_metadata$predictors == "type"]
  stopifnot(length(expected_n) == 1L, nrow(frame) == expected_n,
            all(is.finite(frame$log10_range)))
  raw <- data.frame(type = as.character(frame$interaction_type),
                    value = 10^frame$log10_range)
  raw$position <- match(raw$type, names(type_labels))

  # Estimated means and contrasts of the measure; the estimates sit beside each violin
  em <- estimated_means[estimated_means$measure == measure &
                          estimated_means$predictors == "type", , drop = FALSE]
  ct <- main_contrasts[main_contrasts$measure == measure &
                         main_contrasts$predictors == "type", , drop = FALSE]
  stopifnot(nrow(em) == 4L, all(em$geometric_lower <= em$geometric_estimate),
            all(em$geometric_estimate <= em$geometric_upper))
  type_letters <- compact_letters(ct, em)
  em$position <- match(em$interaction_type, names(type_labels)) + 0.23
  em$letter <- unname(type_letters[em$interaction_type])
  em$letter_y <- em$geometric_upper * 1.55

  # Sample size above each violin
  n_labels <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(type_labels), function(type) {
    values <- raw$value[raw$type == type]
    data.frame(position = match(type, names(type_labels)),
               y = max(values) * 1.40, label = paste0("n = ", length(values)))
  }))

  # scale_y_log10() transforms the observations before the density and box summaries,
  # so the violin shape and the 1.5-IQR whiskers are calculated on log10 values.
  ggplot(raw, aes(position, value, group = type, fill = type)) +
    # Observed ranges: violins with boxes
    geom_violin(scale = "width", trim = TRUE, width = 0.86, alpha = 0.35, colour = NA) +
    geom_boxplot(width = 0.15, fill = "white", colour = "grey30",
                 linewidth = 0.4, outlier.size = 0.55, outlier.alpha = 0.65) +

    # Model estimates with intervals, compact letters and sample sizes
    geom_errorbar(data = em, aes(x = position, ymin = geometric_lower, ymax = geometric_upper),
                  inherit.aes = FALSE, width = 0.11, linewidth = 0.55, colour = "black") +
    geom_point(data = em,
               aes(x = position, y = geometric_estimate, shape = "Model estimate (95% CI)"),
               inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 2.1, colour = "black") +
    geom_text(data = em, aes(x = position, y = letter_y, label = letter),
              inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 3.6, vjust = 0, colour = "black") +
    geom_text(data = n_labels, aes(x = position, y = y, label = label),
              inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 3.0, vjust = 0) +

    # Scales, labels and theme
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq_along(type_labels), labels = unname(type_labels),
                       limits = c(0.5, 4.55), expand = expansion(mult = 0)) +
    scale_y_log10(labels = scales::label_number(big.mark = ",",
                                                scale_cut = scales::cut_short_scale()),
                  expand = expansion(mult = c(0.035, 0.07))) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = type_colours, guide = "none") +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c("Model estimate (95% CI)" = 18), name = NULL) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = titles[[measure]]) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12.5) +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
          axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10.5, angle = 30, hjust = 1),
          axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10.5),
          plot.title = element_text(size = 12.5, hjust = 0.5),
          legend.position = "bottom", legend.text = element_text(size = 11),
          plot.margin = margin(8, 7, 4, 20))
})

# --- Figure 2 ---
fig <- wrap_plots(panels, nrow = 1, guides = "collect") +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A") &
  theme(plot.tag = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14), legend.position = "bottom")
save_report_figure(fig, "plot_range_by_interaction_type", 10.6, 4.3)
```

# Interaction-trait maps (Figure 1)

The strict-cleaning records of the analysed units are summarised in 500-km Equal Earth cells: type proportions (cells with at least 10 classified species), mean recorded partner breadth (at least 5 breadth-known associated species) and median range area (at least 10 species with a range). Figure 1 is drawn from the written cell table.

*Inputs:* s03/species_table.csv; s02/records_final.rds  
*Outputs:* interaction_cells_500km.csv (per cell: classified species, type proportions, mean recorded partner breadth, median range area); plot_interaction_maps.png (Figure 1)

```{r interaction_cells}
# --- Records of the analysed units ---
d <- read_species_table()
tab <- as.data.table(d)
map_cell_km <- 500

# Unique strict-cleaning coordinates of each analysed unit
x <- readRDS(file.path(dir_s02, "records_final.rds"))
x <- unique(x[in_strict_plus == TRUE & !is.na(pool_key) & pool_key %in% tab$pool_key,
              .(pool_key, decimalLongitude, decimalLatitude)])
invisible(gc())

# --- Occupied 500-km cells of each unit, with its type and partner breadth ---
occ <- split(as.data.frame(x[, .(decimalLongitude, decimalLatitude)]), x$pool_key)
rm(x)
invisible(gc())
pres <- equal_area_species_cells(occ, cell_km = map_cell_km)
pres$interaction_type <- as.character(tab$interaction_type)[match(pres$species, tab$pool_key)]
pres$host_breadth <- tab$host_breadth[match(pres$species, tab$pool_key)]

# --- Summary of each cell ---
# Type proportions need at least 10 classified species in a cell (the denominator), and the mean
# partner breadth at least five associated species with a recorded breadth.
one_per_cell <- pres[!duplicated(pres[c("species", "cell_id")]), ]
cells <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(one_per_cell, one_per_cell$cell_id), function(x) {
  classified <- !is.na(x$interaction_type) & x$interaction_type %in% c("n", "f", "m", "p")
  n_classified <- sum(classified)
  denominator <- if (n_classified >= 10L) n_classified else NA_real_
  breadth <- x$host_breadth[!is.na(x$interaction_type) & x$interaction_type != "n" &
                              is.finite(x$host_breadth)]
  data.frame(
    # Cell id and mean coordinates of its rows
    cell_id = x$cell_id[1],
    decimalLongitude = mean(x$decimalLongitude),
    decimalLatitude = mean(x$decimalLatitude),

    # Species counts and classification coverage
    n_total = length(unique(x$species)),
    n_classified = n_classified,
    n_breadth_known = length(breadth),
    coverage = n_classified / length(unique(x$species)),

    # Type proportions among the classified species
    prop_non_associated = sum(x$interaction_type[classified] == "n") / denominator,
    prop_facultative = sum(x$interaction_type[classified] == "f") / denominator,
    prop_mutualist = sum(x$interaction_type[classified] == "m") / denominator,
    prop_parasitic = sum(x$interaction_type[classified] == "p") / denominator,

    # Mean recorded partner breadth of the associated species
    mean_partner_breadth = if (length(breadth) >= 5L) mean(breadth) else NA_real_,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}))
cells <- merge(cells,
               unique(pres[, c("cell_id", "cell_x", "cell_y",
                               "cell_longitude", "cell_latitude")]),
               by = "cell_id")

# --- Median range area ---
# Median range area of the species with a range estimate (>= 10 unique localities), in cells
# with >= 10 of them.
pres$range_area <- tab$range_area[match(pres$species, tab$pool_key)]
med <- as.data.table(pres)[is.finite(range_area) & range_area > 0,
                           .(n_range = .N, median_range_area = median(range_area)),
                           by = cell_id]
med[n_range < 10, median_range_area := NA]
cells <- merge(cells, med, by = "cell_id", all.x = TRUE)

# --- Write the cell table ---
cells_file <- file.path(dir_data_intermediate,
                        paste0("interaction_cells_", map_cell_km, "km.csv"))
write_table(cells, cells_file)
```

## Figure 1

```{r plot_figure_1}
# Drawn from the written cell table, so the figure shows exactly the published values. Panels
# A-D show the proportions of the four types on square-root colour scales whose limits span the
# 1st to 99th percentile of each panel's cells (a common 0-1 scale would leave most cells of the
# obligate panels in the lightest colours); more extreme cells take the end colour, which the
# legend marks with "≤" or "≥". Panel E shows the median range area and F the mean recorded
# ant-genus breadth per associated species.
cells <- read.csv(cells_file)
layers <- map_layers(equal_area_cell_polygons(cells, cell_km = 500))

# --- Colour scales of the proportion panels ---
# Limits: the 1st and 99th percentiles of the cells' proportions, rounded outwards to 0.1
proportion_limits <- function(x) {
  x <- x[is.finite(x)]
  stopifnot(length(x) > 0L, all(x >= 0 & x <= 1))
  q <- stats::quantile(x, c(0.01, 0.99), names = FALSE)

  # round() guards against floating-point noise before rounding outwards to 0.1
  c(max(0, floor(round(q[1] * 10, 6)) / 10), min(1, ceiling(round(q[2] * 10, 6)) / 10))
}

# Breaks and labels for the limits; the end label carries "≤" or "≥" when cells beyond the
# limit take the end colour. Returns a list with `breaks` and `labels`.
proportion_breaks <- function(limits, x) {
  # Intermediate breaks, chosen by the limits
  inner <- if (limits[1] > 0) c(0.5, 0.7) else
    if (limits[2] <= 0.2) c(0.025, 0.05, 0.1) else
    if (limits[2] <= 0.4) c(0.05, 0.1, 0.2) else
    c(0.1, 0.2, 0.4)
  breaks <- sort(unique(c(limits[1],
                          inner[inner > limits[1] & inner < limits[2]],
                          limits[2])))

  # Labels, marked where cells beyond a limit take the end colour
  labels <- format(breaks, trim = TRUE, drop0trailing = TRUE)
  if (min(x, na.rm = TRUE) < limits[1]) labels[1] <- paste("≤", labels[1])
  if (max(x, na.rm = TRUE) > limits[2])
    labels[length(labels)] <- paste("≥", labels[length(labels)])
  list(breaks = breaks, labels = labels)
}

# --- Panels ---
# A-D: type proportions; E: median range area; F: mean recorded partner breadth
variables <- c("prop_non_associated", "prop_facultative", "prop_mutualist",
               "prop_parasitic", "median_range_area", "mean_partner_breadth")
titles <- c("Non-ant-associated", "Facultative", "Obligate mutualist",
            "Obligate parasite", "Median range area (km²)", "Mean recorded ant-genus breadth")
panels <- lapply(seq_along(variables), function(i) {
  v <- layers$cells[[variables[i]]]
  if (i <= 4L) {
    # Proportions: square-root scale between the 1st and 99th percentiles
    limits <- proportion_limits(v)
    scale <- proportion_breaks(limits, v)
    panel <- plot_grid_map(layers, variables[i], NULL, palette = magma_colours,
                           trans = "sqrt", limits = limits,
                           breaks = scale$breaks, labels = scale$labels)
  } else if (i == 5L) {
    # Median range area: logarithmic scale
    breaks <- c(3e5, 1e6, 3e6, 1e7, 3e7)
    panel <- plot_grid_map(layers, variables[i], NULL,
                           palette = magma_colours, trans = "log10", breaks = breaks,
                           labels = scales::label_number(
                             scale_cut = scales::cut_short_scale())(breaks))
  } else {
    # Mean partner breadth: linear scale
    panel <- plot_grid_map(layers, variables[i], NULL, palette = magma_colours,
                           breaks = seq(2, 8, by = 2))
  }

  # Panel title and letter, with a vertical colour bar at the right of each map
  panel + labs(title = titles[i], tag = LETTERS[i]) +
    guides(fill = guide_colourbar(barwidth = grid::unit(2.4, "mm"),
                                  barheight = grid::unit(24, "mm"))) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 9.5, hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(b = 2)),
          plot.tag = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
          legend.position = "right", legend.text = element_text(size = 7.5),
          legend.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0), legend.box.spacing = grid::unit(2, "pt"),
          plot.margin = margin(2, 3, 2, 3))
})

# --- Figure 1 ---
save_report_figure(wrap_plots(panels, ncol = 2), "plot_interaction_maps", 6.9, 5.3)
cat("cells:", nrow(cells), "\n")
```

# Breadth and robustness figures (Figures 3, 4 and S8)

Figure 3 draws range against recorded ant genera from the saved breadth models. Figures 4 and S8 show the range-area contrasts of the robustness table plus the rarefied ranges of `s05_check_robustness`.

*Inputs:* s04/main_models.rds, s04/main_metadata.csv; robustness.csv; s05/rarefied_models.csv  
*Outputs:* plot_range_by_partner_breadth.png, plot_robustness_core_analyses.png, plot_robustness_mutualist_contrasts.png

## Figure 3

```{r plot_figure_3}
# Points are species, jittered horizontally (fixed seed) so that the many species with one or two
# recorded genera are visible, with parasites drawn last. Lines and 95% confidence bands are
# fixed-effect predictions of the additive taxonomic breadth models (common slope, type-specific
# intercepts). Each type's line is solid where at least five species of that type have that
# breadth or more, and dashed beyond.

# --- Saved breadth models ---
models <- readRDS(file.path(dir_s04, "main_models.rds"))
metadata <- read.csv(file.path(dir_s04, "main_metadata.csv"))
titles <- c(area = "Range area (km²)", lat = "Latitudinal extent (km)",
            lon = "Longitudinal extent (km)")
type_labels <- c(f = "Facultative", m = "Obligate mutualist", p = "Obligate parasite")

# --- Panels, one per range measure ---
panels <- lapply(names(titles), function(m) {
  model <- models[[paste0(m, "_breadth")]]
  mf <- model.frame(model)

  # Recorded ant genera of each species: the centred breadth plus the sample mean (whole numbers)
  bm <- metadata$partner_breadth_mean[metadata$measure == m &
                                        metadata$predictors == "breadth"]
  stopifnot(length(bm) == 1L)
  breadth <- mf$partner_breadth_centered + bm
  stopifnot(all(abs(breadth - round(breadth)) < 1e-6))

  # Observations with horizontal jitter; parasites come last, so they are drawn on top
  dd <- data.frame(host_breadth = round(breadth),
                   log10_range = mf$log10_range,
                   interaction_type = factor(as.character(mf$interaction_type),
                                             levels = c("f", "m", "p")))
  set.seed(20261012)
  dd$x <- dd$host_breadth + stats::runif(nrow(dd), -0.18, 0.18)
  dd <- dd[order(match(dd$interaction_type, c("f", "m", "p"))), ]

  # Fixed-effect predictions of each type over its observed breadths, with 95% bands. The line
  # is solid up to the largest breadth that at least five species of the type reach or exceed.
  pr <- do.call(rbind, lapply(levels(dd$interaction_type), function(ty) {
    obs <- dd$host_breadth[dd$interaction_type == ty]
    values <- sort(unique(obs))
    supported <- max(values[vapply(values, function(v) sum(obs >= v) >= 5, TRUE)])
    grid <- if (diff(range(obs)) == 0) unique(obs) else
      seq(min(obs), max(obs), length.out = 120)
    nd <- data.frame(interaction_type = factor(ty, levels = levels(mf$interaction_type)),
                     partner_breadth_centered = grid - bm)
    X <- model.matrix(
      stats::delete.response(stats::terms(reformulas::nobars(stats::formula(model)))), nd)
    b <- lme4::fixef(model)
    X <- X[, names(b), drop = FALSE]
    f <- as.numeric(X %*% b)
    se <- sqrt(diag(X %*% as.matrix(stats::vcov(model)) %*% t(X)))
    data.frame(host_breadth = grid, interaction_type = ty, est = 10^f,
               lo = 10^(f - 1.96 * se), hi = 10^(f + 1.96 * se),
               part = ifelse(grid <= supported + 1e-9, "solid", "dashed"))
  }))
  pr$interaction_type <- factor(pr$interaction_type, levels = c("f", "m", "p"))

  # The dashed part starts where the solid part ends: the last solid point is repeated as dashed
  joins <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(pr, pr$interaction_type), function(x) {
    if (!any(x$part == "dashed")) return(NULL)
    y <- x[x$part == "solid", ][sum(x$part == "solid"), ]
    y$part <- "dashed"
    y
  }))
  pr <- rbind(pr, joins)

  # Points, confidence bands and fitted lines
  ggplot(dd, aes(x, 10^log10_range, colour = interaction_type)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.45, size = 0.8, shape = 16) +
    geom_ribbon(data = pr[pr$part == "solid", ],
                aes(host_breadth, ymin = lo, ymax = hi, fill = interaction_type),
                inherit.aes = FALSE, alpha = 0.12) +
    geom_line(data = pr, aes(host_breadth, est, colour = interaction_type, linetype = part),
              inherit.aes = FALSE, linewidth = 0.7) +

    # Scales, labels and theme
    scale_linetype_manual(values = c(solid = "solid", dashed = "22"), guide = "none") +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1, 2, 5, 10, 15)) +
    scale_y_log10(labels = scales::label_number(scale_cut = scales::cut_short_scale())) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = type_colours[c("f", "m", "p")], labels = type_labels,
                        name = "Interaction type") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = type_colours[c("f", "m", "p")], guide = "none") +
    labs(x = "Recorded ant genera", y = titles[[m]]) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), axis.text = element_text(size = 12))
})

# --- Figure 3 ---
fig <- wrap_plots(panels, nrow = 1, guides = "collect") +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A") &
  theme(plot.tag = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14), legend.position = "bottom")
save_report_figure(fig, "plot_range_by_partner_breadth", 10, 3.8)
```

## Figures 4 and S8

The rows are the robustness table plus the rarefied ranges (ten random localities per species, 200 draws, taxonomic model). `robustness_forest_plot()` draws the range-area effects of the core analyses; it draws Figure 4 (parasite contrasts and breadth) and Figure S8 (the other contrasts).

```{r define_robustness_forest_plot}
#' Draw the publication comparison of range-area effects across the core analyses
#'
#' One row per analysis, grouped by the alternative explanation it addresses (group labels at
#' the left). The three phylogenetic analyses are shown on both trees, Yumnam (main) and Schär
#' (alternative topology), in adjacent rows, and the row labels give the number of species (or
#' genus-by-type units) and of parasites in the type model. Rows marked * have residuals
#' without positive spatial autocorrelation (spatial and joint models; Table S6). Interaction
#' contrasts are range-area ratios on logarithmic axes. The recorded-ant-genus slope is the
#' percentage change in range area, its estimate and interval transformed together as
#' 100 * (ratio - 1). Main Figure 4 shows the two parasite contrasts and breadth; Figure S8 the
#' contrasts involving obligate mutualists and facultative / non-associated, with the same
#' rows.
#' @param robustness Data frame with analysis, measure, contrast, n, n_parasite, ratio, lower,
#'   upper and p columns: the publication robustness table plus the rarefied-range rows
#'   (analysis "rarefied_k10").
#' @param contrasts Named panel titles, in panel order; names are contrast keys ("f-p", ...) or
#'   "breadth".
#' @param base_size Base text size, in points.
#' @param shared_axis Use one logarithmic axis for all ratio panels.
#' @return A patchwork plot. No analyses are fitted and the input is unchanged.
robustness_forest_plot <- function(
    robustness,
    contrasts = c(`f-p` = "Facultative / parasite", `n-p` = "Non-associated / parasite",
                  breadth = "Per recorded ant genus"),
    base_size = 11, shared_axis = FALSE) {
  # --- Rows of the figure ---
  # Analysis, label and group of each row, in plotting order
  rows <- data.frame(
    analysis = c("lmm", "spherical_gam", "pgls_grafted_yumnam_2025", "pgls_grafted_schar_2018",
                 "phylo_spatial_yumnam_2025", "phylo_spatial_schar_2018",
                 "pgls_genus_yumnam_2025", "pgls_genus_schar_2018", "rarefied_k10",
                 "modelled_ranges_daru"),
    label = c("Taxonomic LMM (main)", "Spatial GAM*", "Species PGLS, Yumnam",
              "Species PGLS, Schär", "Joint GAM, Yumnam*", "Joint GAM, Schär*",
              "Genus PGLS, Yumnam", "Genus PGLS, Schär", "Rarefied ranges",
              "Modelled ranges"),
    group = c("Reference", "Space", "Phylogeny", "Phylogeny", "Phylogeny\n+ space",
              "Phylogeny\n+ space", "Genus\nweighting", "Genus\nweighting",
              "Range\nestimate", "Range\nestimate"))

  # --- Range-area estimates of the plotted analyses ---
  required <- c("analysis", "measure", "contrast", "n", "n_parasite", "ratio", "lower",
                "upper", "p")
  if (!all(required %in% names(robustness)))
    stop("Robustness table is missing required columns")
  dat <- as.data.frame(robustness)
  dat <- dat[dat$measure == "area" & dat$analysis %in% rows$analysis &
               dat$contrast %in% names(contrasts), , drop = FALSE]
  if (anyDuplicated(dat[c("analysis", "contrast")]))
    stop("More than one range-area estimate per analysis and contrast")
  if (!nrow(dat) || any(!is.finite(as.matrix(dat[c("ratio", "lower", "upper")]))))
    stop("Range-area effects must have finite estimates and intervals")
  if (any(dat$lower <= 0 | dat$lower > dat$ratio | dat$ratio > dat$upper))
    stop("Range-area ratios must be positive with ordered intervals")

  # Row labels carry the type-model sample: species (or genus-by-type units) / parasites.
  size_rows <- as.data.frame(robustness)
  size_rows <- size_rows[size_rows$measure == "area" & size_rows$contrast == "f-p", ]
  sizes <- size_rows[match(rows$analysis, size_rows$analysis), c("n", "n_parasite")]
  if (any(!is.finite(as.matrix(sizes))))
    stop("Every row needs its type-model sample size and number of parasites")
  rows$label <- sprintf("%s  %d/%d", rows$label, as.integer(sizes$n), as.integer(sizes$n_parasite))
  rows$label <- factor(rows$label, levels = rev(rows$label))
  rows$group <- factor(rows$group, levels = unique(rows$group))

  # Estimates joined to the rows; filled points are significant at p < 0.05
  dat <- merge(dat, rows, by = "analysis")
  dat$significance <- factor(ifelse(dat$p < 0.05, "p < 0.05", "p ≥ 0.05"),
                             levels = c("p < 0.05", "p ≥ 0.05"))

  # Common range of the ratio axes (used when `shared_axis` is TRUE)
  ratio_keys <- setdiff(names(contrasts), "breadth")
  common <- range(c(1, unlist(dat[dat$contrast %in% ratio_keys, c("lower", "upper")])))

  # --- One panel per contrast ---
  panels <- lapply(seq_along(contrasts), function(i) {
    # Estimates of this contrast
    key <- names(contrasts)[i]
    d <- dat[dat$contrast == key, , drop = FALSE]
    if (!nrow(d)) stop("No range-area results for contrast ", key)

    # Keep every row (and its group strip) in every panel, also where a contrast is not
    # estimated
    missing_rows <- rows[!rows$analysis %in% d$analysis, ]
    is_breadth <- key == "breadth"

    # Axis: percentage change for breadth, logarithmic ratio axis for the contrasts
    if (is_breadth) {
      d[c("estimate", "interval_low", "interval_high")] <-
        100 * (d[c("ratio", "lower", "upper")] - 1)

      # Limits in steps of 10 percentage points, including 0
      limits <- c(floor(min(0, d$interval_low) / 10) * 10,
                  ceiling(max(0, d$interval_high) / 10) * 10)
      if (diff(limits) == 0) limits[2] <- limits[1] + 10
      x_scale <- ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(
        limits = limits, breaks = seq(limits[1], limits[2], by = 10),
        labels = function(x) paste0(format(x, trim = TRUE), "%"),
        expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = 0.04))
      reference <- 0
    } else {
      d$estimate <- d$ratio
      d$interval_low <- d$lower
      d$interval_high <- d$upper

      # Limits from this panel or shared by all ratio panels; ticks within them
      limits <- if (shared_axis) common else range(c(1, d$lower, d$upper))
      ticks <- c(0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100)
      ticks <- ticks[ticks >= limits[1] & ticks <= limits[2]]
      x_scale <- ggplot2::scale_x_log10(limits = limits, breaks = ticks,
                                        labels = scales::label_number(),
                                        expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = 0.06))
      reference <- 1
    }

    # Estimates with intervals and a reference line
    p <- ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(estimate, label)) +
      ggplot2::geom_blank(data = missing_rows, ggplot2::aes(y = label),
                          inherit.aes = FALSE) +
      ggplot2::geom_vline(xintercept = reference, colour = "grey55", linewidth = 0.3) +
      ggplot2::geom_errorbar(ggplot2::aes(xmin = interval_low, xmax = interval_high),
                             width = 0.32, linewidth = 0.35, orientation = "y") +
      ggplot2::geom_point(ggplot2::aes(fill = significance), shape = 21, size = 2,
                          stroke = 0.5, show.legend = TRUE) +

      # Fill by significance, axes, and one strip per group of rows
      ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = c(`p < 0.05` = "black", `p ≥ 0.05` = "white"),
                                 name = NULL, drop = FALSE) +
      ggplot2::scale_y_discrete() + x_scale +
      ggplot2::facet_grid(group ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y", switch = "y") +

      # Labels and theme
      ggplot2::labs(title = unname(contrasts[i]), tag = LETTERS[i], y = NULL,
                    x = if (is_breadth) "Increase in range area (95% CI)" else
                      "Range-area ratio (95% CI)") +
      ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = base_size) +
      ggplot2::theme(panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(),
                     panel.grid.major.y = ggplot2::element_line(colour = "grey92",
                                                                linewidth = 0.3),
                     panel.spacing.y = grid::unit(5, "pt"),

                     strip.placement = "outside",
                     strip.text.y.left = ggplot2::element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 1,
                                                               face = "bold",
                                                               size = base_size * 0.82,
                                                               colour = "grey30"),

                     plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(size = base_size, hjust = 0.5),
                     plot.tag = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
                     legend.position = "bottom")

    # Only the first panel keeps the row labels and group strips
    if (i > 1L) p <- p + ggplot2::theme(axis.text.y = ggplot2::element_blank(),
                                        strip.text.y.left = ggplot2::element_blank())
    p
  })
  patchwork::wrap_plots(panels, nrow = 1, guides = "collect") &
    ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom")
}
```

```{r plot_figures_4_and_s8}
# --- Robustness table plus the rarefied ranges ---
robustness <- read.csv(file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "robustness.csv"))
rare <- read.csv(file.path(dir_s05, "rarefied_models.csv"))
rare <- rare[rare$model == "lmm" & rare$sampling == "k10" & rare$ranges == "rarefied", ]

# n-f is shown as facultative / non-associated (f-n): ratio and interval inverted
flip <- rare$contrast == "n-f"
rare[flip, c("ratio", "lower", "upper")] <- 1 / rare[flip, c("ratio", "upper", "lower")]
rare$contrast[flip] <- "f-n"
rare$analysis <- "rarefied_k10"
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(rare[c("measure", "contrast")]),
          all(c("f-p", "n-p", "breadth") %in% rare$contrast))

# Append the rarefied rows to the robustness table (columns not in both are dropped or NA)
rare <- rare[intersect(names(robustness), names(rare))]
for (column in setdiff(names(robustness), names(rare))) rare[[column]] <- NA
robustness <- rbind(robustness, rare[names(robustness)])

# --- Figure 4: parasite contrasts and breadth ---
save_report_figure(robustness_forest_plot(robustness), "plot_robustness_core_analyses",
                   10, 5.8)

# --- Figure S8: the other contrasts, on one shared axis ---
forest_s8 <- robustness_forest_plot(
  robustness,
  contrasts = c(`m-p` = "Mutualist / parasite",
                `f-m` = "Facultative / mutualist",
                `n-m` = "Non-associated / mutualist",
                `f-n` = "Facultative / non-associated"),
  shared_axis = TRUE)
save_report_figure(forest_s8, "plot_robustness_mutualist_contrasts", 11, 5.8)
```

# Supporting Information tables

Evidence basis and attrition by interaction type; type contrasts under four alternative coding decisions; the scale of the evidence ledger and Cohen's kappa against the earlier manual compilation; classification coverage within and outside southern Africa; and the share of obligate species among co-occurring lycaenids.

*Inputs:* s03/ species_table.csv, species_table_daru.csv, species_table_assumed_subtype.csv; s01/ species_traits.csv, evidence_ledger.csv, legacy_comparison.csv; s04/ species_centres.csv, presence_200km.csv  
*Outputs:* si_evidence_basis.csv, si_attrition.csv, si_alternative_decisions.csv, si_alternative_counts.csv, si_ledger_summary.csv, si_legacy_agreement.csv, si_classification_coverage.csv, si_background_contamination.csv

```{r supplement_inputs}
# Main species table, with the trait status of each species
keys <- c("pool_key", "gbif_key")
d <- read_species_table(key_columns = keys)
tr <- fread(file.path(dir_s01, "species_traits.csv"), na.strings = c("", "NA"),
            colClasses = "character")
d$status <- tr$interaction_type_status[match(d$gbif_key, tr$gbif_key)]

# Sample of the main models: classified species with a positive range, a genus and a subfamily
md <- d[!is.na(d$interaction_type) & is.finite(d$range_area) & d$range_area > 0 &
          !is.na(d$genus) & !is.na(d$subfamily), ]
```

## Evidence basis of the analysed interaction types

```{r si_evidence_basis}
# Evidence basis of each analysed species: species-specific evidence, a genus-wide presumption
# stated in a source, or a statement for the species without direct observation
md$evidence <- ifelse(
  md$interaction_type_basis %in% c("direct", "direct_class_inferred_subtype"),
  "Species-specific source evidence",
  ifelse(md$status %in% "presumed_genus_level",
         "Genus-wide presumption stated in a source",
         "Stated for the species in a source (no direct observation)"))

# Species by evidence basis and interaction type, with row totals
ev <- dcast(as.data.table(md)[, .N, by = .(evidence, interaction_type)],
            evidence ~ interaction_type, value.var = "N", fill = 0)
ev[, total := rowSums(.SD), .SDcols = intersect(c("n", "f", "m", "p"), names(ev))]
write_table(ev, file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "si_evidence_basis.csv"))
```

```{r si_attrition}
dd <- read_species_table("species_table_daru.csv", keys)
att <- rbindlist(lapply(c("n", "f", "m", "p"), function(t) data.table(

  classified = sum(d$interaction_type %in% t),
```

## Alternative data decisions (main models; area and latitude)

The main models are refitted under four alternative coding decisions.

```{r si_alternative_decisions}
# --- Refit under an alternative coding ---
# Refits the area and latitude models on the species table `x` and returns their type contrasts
# (n-f shown as f-n) and breadth slope with the sample size, labelled by `label`.
alt_fit <- function(x, label) {
  x$interaction_type <- factor(x$interaction_type, levels = c("n", "f", "m", "p"))
  f <- fit_log_range_models(x,
                            measures = c(area = "range_area", lat = "latitudinal_extent"),
                            breadth_scale = "raw")

  # Type contrasts, with n-f shown as f-n
  ct <- as.data.table(f$contrasts)[
    predictors == "type",
    .(measure, contrast = gsub(" ", "", contrast), ratio = range_ratio,
      lower = ratio_lower, upper = ratio_upper, p = p.value)]
  ct[contrast == "n-f",
     `:=`(contrast = "f-n", ratio = 1 / ratio, lower = 1 / upper, upper = 1 / lower)]

  # Breadth slope
  co <- as.data.table(f$coefficients)[
    predictors == "breadth" & term == "partner_breadth_centered",
    .(measure, contrast = "breadth", ratio = range_ratio, lower = ratio_lower,
      upper = ratio_upper, p = p_value)]

  # Sample size of the type model
  n <- as.data.table(f$metadata)[predictors == "type", .(measure, n)]
  r <- merge(rbind(ct, co), n, by = "measure")
  r[, decision := label]
  r
}

# --- Alternative species tables ---
# (1) obligate species whose subtype was assumed rather than documented keep their coded type (the
#     species table built with the alternative subtype rule)
assumed <- read_species_table("species_table_assumed_subtype.csv", keys)

# (2) three ant-fed aphnaeines coded as mutualists
recip <- d
recip$interaction_type <- as.character(recip$interaction_type)
recip$interaction_type[recip$species %in% c("Axiocerses_harpax", "Crudaria_capensis",
                                            "Crudaria_wykehami")] <- "m"

# (3) species-level subtype evidence only: obligate species whose mutualist or parasite subtype
#     rests on a genus statement or on the source's inference from relatives are left
#     unclassified
ledger <- fread(file.path(dir_s01, "evidence_ledger.csv"), colClasses = "character",
                na.strings = c("", "NA"))
species_level <- d
species_level$interaction_type <- as.character(species_level$interaction_type)
species_level$interaction_type[species_level$interaction_type %in% c("m", "p") &
                                 !species_level$interaction_type_basis %in% "direct"] <- NA

# (4) Fiedler (2012) definition: classified species that Fiedler lists as ant parasites (any
#     recorded trophallaxis counts) are coded as parasites
fiedler_keys <- unique(ledger[source_id == "fiedler2012" &
                                claim_type == "interaction_category" & class == "p",
                              accepted_key])
fiedler <- d
fiedler$interaction_type <- as.character(fiedler$interaction_type)
recode <- !is.na(fiedler$interaction_type) &
  (fiedler$gbif_key %in% fiedler_keys | fiedler$pool_key %in% fiedler_keys)
fiedler$interaction_type[recode] <- "p"
cat("species recoded as parasites under Fiedler (2012):", sum(recode & d$interaction_type != "p"),
    "\n")

# --- Refits under the main and the four alternative codings ---
alt <- rbind(alt_fit(d, "main"),
             alt_fit(assumed, "assumed_subtype_as_m"),
             alt_fit(recip, "ant_fed_aphnaeines_as_m"),
             alt_fit(species_level, "species_level_subtype_only"),
             alt_fit(fiedler, "fiedler2012_parasites"))
write_table(alt, file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "si_alternative_decisions.csv"))

# Parasites and mutualists per decision (type model, area).
alt_counts <- rbindlist(lapply(
  list(main = d,
       assumed_subtype_as_m = assumed,
       ant_fed_aphnaeines_as_m = recip,
       species_level_subtype_only = species_level,
       fiedler2012_parasites = fiedler),
  function(x) {
    ok <- !is.na(x$interaction_type) & is.finite(x$range_area) & x$range_area > 0 &
      !is.na(x$genus) & !is.na(x$subfamily)
    data.table(n = sum(ok),
               n_m = sum(ok & x$interaction_type %in% "m"),
               n_p = sum(ok & x$interaction_type %in% "p"))
  }),
  idcol = "decision")
write_table(alt_counts, file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "si_alternative_counts.csv"))
```

## Evidence ledger and agreement with the earlier manual compilation

Cohen's kappa compares the interaction types of the species shared with the 2024 compilation.

```{r si_ledger_agreement}
# Size of the evidence ledger: claims, sources and species
write_table(data.table(claims = nrow(ledger),
                       sources = uniqueN(ledger$source_id),
                       species = uniqueN(ledger$accepted_key[!is.na(ledger$accepted_key)])),
            file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "si_ledger_summary.csv"))

# Types of the species shared with the 2024 compilation, as a confusion table
lc <- fread(file.path(dir_s01, "legacy_comparison.csv"), colClasses = "character",
            na.strings = c("", "NA"))
lc <- lc[legacy_interaction_type %in% c("n", "f", "m", "p") &
           interaction_type %in% c("n", "f", "m", "p")]
agree_tab <- table(factor(lc$legacy_interaction_type, levels = c("n", "f", "m", "p")),
                   factor(lc$interaction_type, levels = c("n", "f", "m", "p")))

# Cohen's kappa from the observed (po) and the chance (pe) agreement
po <- sum(diag(agree_tab)) / sum(agree_tab)
pe <- sum(rowSums(agree_tab) * colSums(agree_tab)) / sum(agree_tab)^2
write_table(data.table(shared = sum(agree_tab), agree = sum(diag(agree_tab)), share = po,
                       kappa = (po - pe) / (1 - pe)),
            file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "si_legacy_agreement.csv"))
```

## Classification coverage by range size, within and outside southern Africa

Southern Africa follows the region rule of the regional robustness check (centre south of 15 S, between 10 and 55 E).

```{r si_classification_coverage}
# Centres of the species with a range, and their region (southern Africa: centre south of
# 15 S and between 10 and 55 E)
centres <- fread(file.path(dir_s04, "species_centres.csv"),
                 colClasses = c(species = "character"))
cov <- d[is.finite(d$range_area) & d$range_area > 0, ]
la <- centres$geo_latitude[match(cov$pool_key, centres$species)]
lo <- centres$geo_longitude[match(cov$pool_key, centres$species)]
cov$region <- ifelse(is.finite(la) & la < -15 & lo > 10 & lo < 55, "southern_Africa", "elsewhere")

# Geometric mean
gm <- function(x) 10^mean(log10(x))

# By region: species with a range, share classified, geometric-mean range area of the
# classified and unclassified species, and parasites
write_table(as.data.table(cov)[,
              .(n = .N,
                classified = sum(!is.na(interaction_type)),
                share_classified = mean(!is.na(interaction_type)),
                gm_area_classified = gm(range_area[!is.na(interaction_type)]),
                gm_area_unclassified = gm(range_area[is.na(interaction_type)]),
                parasites = sum(interaction_type %in% "p")),
              by = region],
            file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "si_classification_coverage.csv"))
```

## Obligate species among co-occurring lycaenids

For each analysed species, the share of the other lycaenid range units in its occupied 200-km cells that are obligate mutualists or parasites (mean over its cells) is summarised by interaction type; a lycaenid background would partly contain the trait under test.

```{r si_background_contamination}
# Species with a range in their occupied 200-km cells, with their interaction type
pres <- fread(file.path(dir_s04, "presence_200km.csv"),
              colClasses = c(species = "character"))[, .(species, cell_id)]
pres <- pres[species %in% d$pool_key[is.finite(d$range_area)]]
pres[, type := as.character(d$interaction_type)[match(species, d$pool_key)]]

# Species, obligate species (m or p) and parasites in each cell
cc <- pres[, .(n_all = .N,
               n_mp = sum(type %in% c("m", "p")),
               n_p = sum(type %in% "p")),
           by = cell_id]

# For each classified species in each of its cells: the other species there (o) and how many of
# them are obligate (o_mp) or parasites (o_p)
fc <- merge(pres[type %in% c("n", "f", "m", "p")], cc, by = "cell_id")
fc[, `:=`(o = n_all - 1,
          o_mp = n_mp - (type %in% c("m", "p")),
          o_p = n_p - (type == "p"))]

# Mean share over the cells of each species, then the mean over the species of each type
cont <- fc[o > 0,
           .(share_mp = mean(o_mp / o), share_p = mean(o_p / o)),
           by = .(species, type)][
  , .(species = .N, share_m_or_p = mean(share_mp), share_p = mean(share_p)), by = type][
  order(match(type, c("n", "f", "m", "p")))]
write_table(cont, file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "si_background_contamination.csv"))
print(alt_counts)
print(cont)
```

# Range accumulation example (Figure S2)

Accumulation of latitudinal extent, longitudinal extent and MCP area with the number of thinned localities of *Celastrina argiolus*, using the thinning of `s02_prepare_ranges`. The curves are recomputed on every run.

*Inputs:* s02/records_final.rds, s02/parameters.csv  
*Outputs:* accumulation_example.csv (the plotted curves); plot_accumulation_example.png

```{r plot_accumulation_example}
# --- Thinning parameters of s02 ---
# The thinning of s02_prepare_ranges (same grid, distance and per-species seed), applied to the
# strict records.
s02_parameters <- read.csv(file.path(dir_s02, "parameters.csv"), colClasses = "character")

# Numeric value of one parameter of s02
parameter <- function(name) {
  v <- s02_parameters$value[s02_parameters$parameter == name]
  stopifnot(length(v) == 1L)
  as.numeric(v)
}

# --- Thinned localities of Celastrina argiolus ---
# GBIF key of Celastrina argiolus
key_ca <- "1925918"
x <- readRDS(file.path(dir_s02, "records_final.rds"))
x <- as.data.frame(unique(x[in_strict_plus == TRUE & x$pool_key == key_ca,
                            .(decimalLongitude, decimalLatitude)]))
invisible(gc())
cell_km <- parameter("thin_cell_km")
th <- thin_species(x, global_thinning_grid(cell_km), cell_km = cell_km,
                   distance_km = parameter("thin_distance_km"),
                   seed = parameter("thin_seed") + as.numeric(key_ca))
cat("thinned localities:", nrow(th), "\n")

# --- Accumulation curves ---
# Each of 1,000 replicates is one random order of the thinned localities, measured on growing
# prefixes of that order, so the samples are nested as in an accumulation curve. Every sample
# uses the species' full-range cylindrical equal-area projection and converts longitude at the
# full range's mid-latitude.
sizes <- sort(unique(as.integer(c(seq(10, nrow(th), by = 50), nrow(th)))))
reference_latitude <- mean(range(th$decimalLatitude))
projection <- species_cea_crs(th$decimalLongitude)
projected <- project_species_cea(th, projection)

# The random orders (fixed seed)
set.seed(20240401L)
orders <- replicate(1000L, sample.int(nrow(projected)), simplify = FALSE)

# Latitudinal extent, longitudinal extent and MCP area (the first three values returned) of every
# prefix; an array of measures x sample sizes x replicates
draws <- simplify2array(lapply(orders, function(order) vapply(sizes, function(n) {
  projected_mcp_extent_area(projected[order[seq_len(n)], , drop = FALSE],
                            longitude_reference_latitude = reference_latitude,
                            projection = projection, include_s2_audit = FALSE)[1:3]
}, numeric(3L))))

# Mean, standard deviation and 95% interval (2.5th and 97.5th percentiles) of each measure at
# each sample size
curve <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(sizes), function(i) {
  # Measures x replicates
  values <- draws[, i, ]
  data.frame(n_records = sizes[i],
             measure = c("latitudinal_extent", "longitudinal_extent", "range_area"),
             mean = rowMeans(values),
             sd = apply(values, 1, stats::sd),
             lower = apply(values, 1, stats::quantile, probs = 0.025),
             upper = apply(values, 1, stats::quantile, probs = 0.975),
             row.names = NULL)
}))
curve_file <- file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "accumulation_example.csv")
write_table(curve, curve_file)

# --- Figure S2 ---
# The figure is drawn from the written curves.
curve <- read.csv(curve_file)
curve$measure <- factor(curve$measure,
                        levels = c("latitudinal_extent", "longitudinal_extent", "range_area"),
                        labels = c("Latitudinal extent (km)", "Longitudinal extent (km)",
                                   "Range area (km²)"))
panels <- lapply(levels(curve$measure), function(measure) {
  ggplot(curve[curve$measure == measure, ], aes(n_records, mean)) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = pmax(0, mean - sd), ymax = mean + sd), fill = "grey75",
                alpha = 0.65) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.45) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_number(scale_cut = scales::cut_short_scale())) +
    labs(x = "Number of thinned localities", y = measure) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
})
fig <- wrap_plots(panels, nrow = 1) + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A") &
  theme(plot.tag = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11))
save_report_figure(fig, "plot_accumulation_example", 9.3, 3.4)
```

## Figure S4

```{r plot_figure_s4}
# --- Occupied 500-km cells of the species with a range ---
map_cell_km <- 500
x <- readRDS(file.path(dir_s02, "records_final.rds"))
units <- d$pool_key[is.finite(d$range_area)]

              .(pool_key, decimalLongitude, decimalLatitude)])

rm(x)
invisible(gc())
pres <- equal_area_species_cells(occ, cell_km = map_cell_km)
pres$area <- d$range_area[match(pres$species, d$pool_key)]

# Richness and median range area of each cell (median only where there are 10 or more species)
cells <- as.data.table(pres)[, .(richness = .N,
                                 median_area = median(area),
                                 cell_x = cell_x[1],
                                 cell_y = cell_y[1],
                                 longitude = cell_longitude[1],
                                 latitude = cell_latitude[1]),
                             by = cell_id]
cells[richness < 10, median_area := NA]
cells[, log10_median_area := log10(median_area)]

# --- Cells of the maps ---
# Recorded species per cell and the share with an interaction classification come from the cells
# of Figure 1; both describe sampling and data coverage.
ic <- read.csv(file.path(dir_data_intermediate,
                         paste0("interaction_cells_", map_cell_km, "km.csv")))
cells_all <- merge(as.data.frame(cells)[, c("cell_id", "cell_x", "cell_y", "richness",
                                            "log10_median_area")],
                   ic[, c("cell_id", "cell_x", "cell_y", "n_total", "coverage",
                          "mean_partner_breadth")],
                   by = c("cell_id", "cell_x", "cell_y"), all = TRUE)

# Share of the recorded species with a range estimate
cells_all$prop_range <- cells_all$richness / cells_all$n_total
layers <- map_layers(equal_area_cell_polygons(cells_all, map_cell_km))

# --- Panels ---
# One sequential palette for all panels (magma, light = low, dark = high; colour-blind safe, not
# red-green).
s4_tag <- function(p, tag)
  p + labs(tag = tag) + theme(plot.tag = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11))
s4a <- s4_tag(plot_grid_map(layers, "n_total", "Recorded species", magma_colours,
                            trans = "log10"),
              "A")

# B and C on linear scales: both shares are concentrated near 1, where a square-root scale
# would compress the differences. C is truncated at 0.5 (lower cells take the lightest colour)
# so that cells with incomplete range coverage stand out.
s4b <- s4_tag(plot_grid_map(layers, "coverage",
                            "Recorded species with an interaction classification",
                            magma_colours,
                            limits = c(0, 1), breaks = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1)),

                            "Recorded species with a range estimate (≥ 10 localities)",

                            limits = c(0.5, 1), breaks = c(0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8, 0.9, 1),
                            labels = c("≤ 0.5", "0.6", "0.7", "0.8", "0.9", "1")),
              "C")

# --- Figure S4 ---
# A and B side by side; C below, centred
fig_s4 <- wrap_plots((s4a | s4b),
                     (plot_spacer() + s4c + plot_spacer() +
                        plot_layout(widths = c(1, 2, 1))),
                     ncol = 1)
save_report_figure(fig_s4, "plot_richness_range_maps", 9.2, 5.8)
```

## Figure S5

The spatial term of the main-sample spherical GAM is mapped at the cell centres, in cells with at least three species with a range.

```{r plot_figure_s5}
# --- Spherical GAM of range area (main sample) ---
ce <- fread(file.path(dir_s04, "species_centres.csv"), colClasses = c(species = "character"))
dg <- merge(as.data.frame(md), ce, by.x = "pool_key", by.y = "species")
gam <- fit_species_spatial_gam(dg, "range_area")

# --- Partial spatial effect at the cell centres ---
# The prediction data place a facultative species, with the subfamily and genus of the first
# modelled species, at each cell centre; only the spatial term is used.
nd <- data.frame(geo_latitude = cells$latitude, geo_longitude = cells$longitude,
                 interaction_type = factor("f", levels = levels(gam$data$interaction_type)),
                 subfamily = gam$data$subfamily[1], genus = gam$data$genus[1])
tt <- predict(gam$model, newdata = nd, type = "terms")
sp_term <- grep("geo_latitude", colnames(tt), value = TRUE)
cells$spatial_effect <- ifelse(cells$richness >= 3, tt[, sp_term], NA)

# --- Figure S5 ---
# Diverging scale, symmetric around zero
layers_g <- map_layers(equal_area_cell_polygons(as.data.frame(cells), map_cell_km))
lim <- max(abs(cells$spatial_effect), na.rm = TRUE)
fig_s5 <- plot_grid_map(layers_g, "spatial_effect", "Partial spatial effect (log10 range area)",
                        palette = c("#B2182B", "#F7F7F7", "#2166AC"), midpoint = 0,
                        limits = c(-lim, lim))
save_report_figure(fig_s5, "plot_gam_spatial_effect", 8.4, 4.6)
```
