# Phylogeny with traits (Figure S7)

The Yumnam & Kodandaramaiah (2025) tree with the interaction types and range areas of the matched species, and the counts quoted in the caption.

*Inputs:* phylogenies/yumnam_2025 tree; s04/crosswalk_yumnam_2025.csv; s03/species_table.csv  
*Outputs:* plot_phylogeny_traits.png; si_phylogeny_overlay_counts.csv

The fan layout of `ape` gives the tip and branch coordinates, which are drawn with `ggplot2`; both panels use the same tree drawing.

```{r define_phylogeny_plots}
#' Obtain plotting coordinates from ape without drawing a base-R figure
#'
#' `ape::plot.phylo()` supplies a stable fan layout; its coordinates are then
#' converted to a data frame for publication styling with ggplot2.
#' @param tree A `phylo` object.
#' @return List containing branch segments, arcs and tip coordinates.
phylogeny_plot_data <- function(tree) {
  # Ladderised tree (right = FALSE: at each node the smaller clade comes first round the fan)
  tree <- ape::ladderize(tree, right = FALSE)

  # ape computes the fan layout on a temporary PDF device, closed and deleted on exit
  temporary <- tempfile(fileext = ".pdf")
  grDevices::pdf(temporary, width = 5, height = 5)
  on.exit({
    grDevices::dev.off()
    unlink(temporary)
  }, add = TRUE)
  ape::plot.phylo(
    tree, type = "fan", use.edge.length = TRUE, show.tip.label = FALSE,
    no.margin = TRUE, plot = FALSE
  )

  # Node coordinates stored by ape, with their radius and angle
  plot_environment <- get(".PlotPhyloEnv", envir = asNamespace("ape"))
  coordinates <- get("last_plot.phylo", envir = plot_environment)
  edges <- tree$edge
  node_x <- coordinates$xx
  node_y <- coordinates$yy
  radius <- sqrt(node_x^2 + node_y^2)
  angle <- atan2(node_y, node_x)

  # A circular phylogram consists of a radial, branch-length-bearing segment
  # plus an arc at the parent's depth. Drawing a single parent-child chord
  # would distort branch length when their angles differ.
  segments <- data.frame(
    x = radius[edges[, 1]] * cos(angle[edges[, 2]]),
    y = radius[edges[, 1]] * sin(angle[edges[, 2]]),
    xend = radius[edges[, 2]] * cos(angle[edges[, 2]]),
    yend = radius[edges[, 2]] * sin(angle[edges[, 2]])
  )

  # Arc of each edge: eight points at the parent's radius, from the parent's angle to the
  # child's by the shorter way round
  arcs <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(edges)), function(i) {
    from <- angle[edges[i, 1]]
    to <- angle[edges[i, 2]]
    difference <- (to - from + pi) %% (2 * pi) - pi
    theta <- seq(from, from + difference, length.out = 8L)
    data.frame(
      edge = i,
      x = radius[edges[i, 1]] * cos(theta),
      y = radius[edges[i, 1]] * sin(theta)
    )
  }))

  # Tip coordinates
  tips <- data.frame(
    tip_label = tree$tip.label,
    x = coordinates$xx[seq_len(ape::Ntip(tree))],
    y = coordinates$yy[seq_len(ape::Ntip(tree))],
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  list(segments = segments, arcs = arcs, tips = tips)
}

#' Draw a clean circular overview of a large phylogeny
#'
#' @param tree A `phylo` object.
#' @param title,subtitle Figure text.
#' @param matches Optional crosswalk table (`matched`, `tree_tip_original`,
#'   `interaction_type`) for tips coloured by interaction type.
#' @param range_overlay Optional table with `tree_tip_original` and positive
#'   `range_area` (km2) for tips coloured by log10 range area.
#' The caller adds the colour scale of the overlay.
#' @param branch_colour Colour used for the published branches.
#' @param scale_unit Label for the published branch-length units. Set to `NULL`
#'   to omit the scale bar.
#' @return A ggplot object.
plot_phylogeny_overview <- function(
    tree, title, subtitle, matches = NULL, range_overlay = NULL,
    branch_colour = "#263238",
    scale_unit = "published branch-length units") {
  # --- Branches ---
  # Arcs and radial segments of the fan layout
  plot_data <- phylogeny_plot_data(tree)
  plot <- ggplot2::ggplot() +
    ggplot2::geom_path(
      data = plot_data$arcs, ggplot2::aes(x, y, group = edge),
      linewidth = 0.13, colour = branch_colour, lineend = "round"
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_segment(
      data = plot_data$segments,
      ggplot2::aes(x, y, xend = xend, yend = yend),
      linewidth = 0.16, colour = branch_colour, lineend = "round"
    ) +

    # Equal aspect, titles and a theme without axes
    ggplot2::coord_equal(clip = "off") +
    ggplot2::labs(title = title, subtitle = subtitle) +
    ggplot2::theme_void(base_size = 10) +
    ggplot2::theme(
      plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
      plot.subtitle = ggplot2::element_text(size = 8.5, colour = "grey30"),

      plot.margin = ggplot2::margin(6, 6, 6, 6)
    )

  # --- Scale bar ---
  # A round length (the first non-zero break of pretty() from 0 to a quarter of the tree
  # radius), at the bottom left
  if (!is.null(scale_unit) && !is.null(tree$edge.length)) {
    radius <- max(sqrt(plot_data$tips$x^2 + plot_data$tips$y^2))
    scale_length <- pretty(c(0, radius / 4), n = 2)[2]
    scale_y <- -1.08 * radius
    scale_x <- -0.92 * radius
    plot <- plot +
      ggplot2::annotate(
        "segment", x = scale_x, xend = scale_x + scale_length,
        y = scale_y, yend = scale_y, linewidth = 0.45, colour = "grey20"
      ) +
      ggplot2::annotate(
        "text", x = scale_x + scale_length / 2, y = scale_y,
        label = paste(format(scale_length, trim = TRUE), scale_unit),
        vjust = -0.7, size = 3.2, colour = "grey20"
      )
  }

  # --- Tips coloured by interaction type ---
  if (!is.null(matches)) {
    # Matched tips with their type
    overlay_matches <- matches[matches$matched, c("tree_tip_original", "interaction_type")]
    names(overlay_matches)[1] <- "matched_tip_label"
    overlay <- merge(
      plot_data$tips,
      overlay_matches,
      by.x = "tip_label", by.y = "matched_tip_label", all = FALSE
    )

    if (nrow(overlay)) {
      overlay$interaction_type <- factor(
        overlay$interaction_type, levels = c("n", "f", "m", "p")
      )
      plot <- plot +
        ggplot2::geom_point(
          data = overlay, ggplot2::aes(x, y, colour = interaction_type),
          size = 0.8, alpha = 0.85
        ) +
        ggplot2::theme(
          legend.position = "bottom",
          legend.key.width = grid::unit(3, "mm"),
          legend.text = ggplot2::element_text(size = 7),
          legend.title = ggplot2::element_text(size = 7.5)
        )
    }
  }

  # --- Tips coloured by log10 range area ---
  if (!is.null(range_overlay)) {
    stopifnot(all(c("tree_tip_original", "range_area") %in%
                    names(range_overlay)))

    # Tips with a positive range area, at most one row per tip
    overlay_matches <- range_overlay[
      is.finite(range_overlay$range_area) & range_overlay$range_area > 0,
      c("tree_tip_original", "range_area"), drop = FALSE
    ]
    if (anyDuplicated(overlay_matches$tree_tip_original)) {
      stop("The range overlay must contain at most one row per curated tip.")
    }

    # Tip coordinates joined to their range areas
    overlay <- merge(plot_data$tips, overlay_matches,
                     by.x = "tip_label", by.y = "tree_tip_original")

    if (nrow(overlay)) {
      overlay$log10_range_area <- log10(overlay$range_area)
      plot <- plot +
        ggplot2::geom_point(
          data = overlay, ggplot2::aes(x, y, colour = log10_range_area),
          size = 0.8, alpha = 0.85
        ) +
        ggplot2::theme(
          legend.position = "bottom",
          legend.text = ggplot2::element_text(size = 7),
          legend.title = ggplot2::element_text(size = 7.5)
        )
    }
  }
  plot
}
```

```{r plot_phylogeny_traits}
# --- Tree and matched species ---
d <- read_species_table(key_columns = c("pool_key", "gbif_key"))
tree <- read_published_tree(
  file.path(dir_data_raw, "phylogenies", "yumnam_2025",
            "21Jan2025_30June23_SubfamAdded_RelTime_DivergenceTime_928sp.nwk"))

# Crosswalk of the analysed species to the tree tips, with their interaction types
cw <- read.csv(file.path(dir_s04, "crosswalk_yumnam_2025.csv"))
cw$interaction_type <- as.character(d$interaction_type)[match(cw$analysis_species, d$species)]

# Matched tips with a type, and matched tips with a range area
cw_type <- cw[cw$matched & !is.na(cw$interaction_type), ]
cw_range <- data.frame(tree_tip_original = cw$tree_tip_original[cw$matched],
                       range_area = d$range_area[match(cw$analysis_species[cw$matched],
                                                       d$species)])
cw_range <- cw_range[is.finite(cw_range$range_area) & cw_range$range_area > 0, ]

# --- Panels A and B ---
# Branch lengths are RelTime divergence times in Myr (root depth 76.2).
f6 <- plot_phylogeny_overview(
  tree, "A  Interaction type",
  sprintf("%d classified species matched to the tree", nrow(cw_type)),
  matches = cw_type, scale_unit = "Myr")
f7 <- plot_phylogeny_overview(
  tree, "B  Range area",
  sprintf("%d species with a range estimate matched to the tree", nrow(cw_range)),
  range_overlay = cw_range, scale_unit = NULL)

# Same colour rule as the maps: dark = larger range; the legend labels are in km2.
rg <- log10(cw_range$range_area)
ticks7 <- seq(ceiling(min(rg)), floor(max(rg)), by = 2)
f7 <- f7 + scale_colour_viridis_c(
  option = "A", direction = -1, begin = 0.15, end = 0.95, breaks = ticks7,
  labels = scales::label_number(big.mark = ",",
                                scale_cut = scales::cut_short_scale())(10^ticks7),
  name = expression("Range area (km"^2*")"),
  guide = guide_colourbar(barwidth = grid::unit(4, "mm"), barheight = grid::unit(30, "mm"),
                          title.position = "top"))

# The trees are stacked, each with its legend in an empty corner, so that they print larger: the
# 7 x 14 inch source is shown about 4.4 inches wide, and text sizes are set for that reduction.
tree_report_theme <- theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
                           plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10.5),
                           legend.text = element_text(size = 10),
                           legend.title = element_text(size = 10.5),
                           legend.position = "inside",
                           legend.position.inside = c(1, 0),
                           legend.justification = c(1, 0))

# Colours of the interaction types, as in the other report figures.
f6 <- f6 + scale_colour_manual(values = type_colours, breaks = c("n", "f", "m", "p"),
                               labels = c("Non-associated", "Facultative", "Mutualist",
                                          "Parasite"),
                               name = "Interaction type", drop = FALSE) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(ncol = 1, title.position = "top",
                               override.aes = list(size = 2.5))) +
  tree_report_theme
f7 <- f7 + tree_report_theme

# --- Labels of the parasitic genera ---
# The text discusses the parasitic genera by name: one label per genus (which may also contain
# non-parasitic species) at the circular mean angle of its matched parasite tips in the fan
# layout.
tip_xy <- phylogeny_plot_data(tree)$tips
parasite_tips <- cw_type[cw_type$interaction_type == "p",
                         c("tree_tip_original", "analysis_species")]
parasite_tips$genus <- d$genus[match(parasite_tips$analysis_species, d$species)]
parasite_tips <- merge(tip_xy, parasite_tips, by.x = "tip_label", by.y = "tree_tip_original")
stopifnot(nrow(parasite_tips) == sum(cw_type$interaction_type == "p"),
          !anyNA(parasite_tips$genus))
tip_radius <- max(sqrt(tip_xy$x^2 + tip_xy$y^2))
genus_labels <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(parasite_tips, parasite_tips$genus), function(g) {
  a <- atan2(g$y, g$x)
  data.frame(genus = g$genus[1], label = g$genus[1], n = nrow(g),
             angle = atan2(mean(sin(a)), mean(cos(a))))
}))

# Neighbouring labels are pushed apart along the circle and joined to their tips by short leader
# lines.
genus_labels <- genus_labels[order(genus_labels$angle), ]
genus_labels$label_angle <- genus_labels$angle
min_gap <- 0.075
for (iteration in 1:200) for (i in seq_len(nrow(genus_labels))[-1]) {
  gap <- genus_labels$label_angle[i] - genus_labels$label_angle[i - 1]
  if (gap < min_gap) {
    genus_labels$label_angle[i - 1] <- genus_labels$label_angle[i - 1] - (min_gap - gap) / 2
    genus_labels$label_angle[i] <- genus_labels$label_angle[i] + (min_gap - gap) / 2
  }
}

# Polar position (radius as a multiple of the tip radius, and angle) as x and y; the leaders run
# from the tips to the pushed-apart label positions
polar <- function(r, a)
  data.frame(x = r * tip_radius * cos(a), y = r * tip_radius * sin(a))
leaders <- cbind(polar(1.012, genus_labels$angle),
                 setNames(polar(1.05, genus_labels$label_angle), c("xend", "yend")))
genus_labels[c("x", "y")] <- polar(1.06, genus_labels$label_angle)

# Text angle in degrees; labels on the left half are turned by 180 degrees and right-aligned
right_side <- cos(genus_labels$label_angle) >= 0
genus_labels$text_angle <- genus_labels$label_angle * 180 / pi + ifelse(right_side, 0, 180)
genus_labels$hjust <- ifelse(right_side, 0, 1)

# Leaders and labels on panel A. Both panels have identical fixed coordinates (equal tree size),
# with room for the radial labels.
tree_limits <- list(x = c(-1.36, 1.36) * tip_radius, y = c(-1.4, 1.36) * tip_radius)
f6 <- f6 + geom_segment(data = leaders, aes(x, y, xend = xend, yend = yend),
                        inherit.aes = FALSE, linewidth = 0.3, colour = "#8E3F72") +
  geom_text(data = genus_labels,
            aes(x, y, label = label, angle = text_angle, hjust = hjust),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 3.1, fontface = "italic", colour = "#8E3F72") +
  coord_equal(xlim = tree_limits$x, ylim = tree_limits$y, expand = FALSE, clip = "off")
f7 <- f7 + coord_equal(xlim = tree_limits$x, ylim = tree_limits$y, expand = FALSE,
                       clip = "off")

# --- Figure S7 ---
# Each panel is wrapped whole so that patchwork lays them out independently (aligning two
# fixed-aspect panels would stretch panel B).
fig <- wrap_elements(full = f6) / wrap_elements(full = f7)

# The figure is drawn in a new R process with the same packages: drawing Figure 3 earlier in this
# session changes how the graphics device sizes the many small tip symbols, so the figure would
# otherwise depend on the order of the sections.
fig_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds")
saveRDS(fig, fig_file)
render_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".R")

# The script of the new process: load the packages and save the figure
writeLines(c("library(ggplot2); library(patchwork)",
             sprintf("ggsave(%s, readRDS(%s), width = 7, height = 14, dpi = 400, bg = 'white', device = ragg::agg_png)",
                     deparse(file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "plot_phylogeny_traits.png")),
                     deparse(fig_file))),
           render_file)

# Run it with the project library, then restore the previous R_LIBS
r_libs <- Sys.getenv("R_LIBS")
Sys.setenv(R_LIBS = paste(.libPaths(), collapse = .Platform$path.sep))
status <- system2(file.path(R.home("bin"), "Rscript"), c("--vanilla", shQuote(render_file)))
Sys.setenv(R_LIBS = r_libs)
stopifnot(status == 0)

# --- Counts quoted in the caption ---
counts <- data.table(classified_on_tree = nrow(cw_type), range_on_tree = nrow(cw_range),
                     tips = length(tree$tip.label))
write_table(counts, file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "si_phylogeny_overlay_counts.csv"))
print(counts)
```
